title: The Wolf and the Lamb

full_text:
A sweet, innocent little lamb, having strayed from the flock, wandered down to a clear mountain brook to quench her thirst. While she was delicately lapping the fresh water, a fierce, ravenous wolf stalked out from the dark pine woods in search of prey.

Eager to devour the tender lamb, yet wishing to justify his savagery with an appearance of justice, the wolf bared his yellow fangs and snarled furiously: "How dare you muddy the water that I am trying to drink, you insolent rascal? Do you have no respect for your elders?"

The trembling lamb bleated gently in reply: "Pardon me, noble sir, but I cannot possibly be muddying your water. You are drinking high up the stream near the spring, while I am standing far below you; the current flows from you down to me!"

Frustrated by her flawless logic, the wolf scowled and barked: "Be that as it may, you are an insolent rogue! Exactly six months ago, you insulted me behind my back with slanderous words!"

"Alas, sir," cried the lamb in tears, "six months ago I was not even born! I am only three months old and still drink my mother's milk."

"If it was not you, then it was your father!" roared the savage brute. "Your entire clan hates wolves, and I shall not be cheated of my dinner!"

Without another word, the wolf sprang upon the defenseless lamb and dragged her into the dark forest, proving that when cruelty has resolved upon a deed, no plea of innocent truth can alter its wicked design.
moral: A tyrant will always invent an excuse for cruelty, and innocence cannot reason with malice.
